title: Starbucks wants a drive-thru menu that recognizes you. It is not live
friendlyTitle: Starbucks wants a drive-thru menu that recognizes you. It is not live
summary: The Verge reports that on Starbucks' latest earnings call, chief executive Brian Niccol said the company will explore experiences that recognize participating customers as they arrive, show a personalized digital menu, and make payment easier. Starting in 2027, Starbucks also plans to test background models at the drive-thru to help baristas enter orders more accurately. The app may later add search and ordering that an agent can do. Niccol said it is early, and that the company will test before it scales.
friendlySummary: The Verge reports that on Starbucks' latest earnings call, chief executive Brian Niccol said the company will explore ways to recognize customers who take part as they arrive, show a menu made for them, and make payment easier. Starting in 2027, Starbucks also plans to test background models at the drive-thru so staff can enter orders more accurately. The app may later add search and ordering that an agent can do. Niccol said it is early, and that the company will test before it rolls anything out widely.
whyItMatters: Nothing changes at the speaker box this week. If you use a Starbucks account, the plan being described is recognition plus a menu built for you, not a chatbot you have to talk to. The part to watch is what 'participating' means, and whether a usual order becomes the default before you have said it.
